page.layout: Running head centred top above the text; page number top left. Left margin notes beside the woodcut (top left, and at the lower left). Woodcut of a figure on a cross at upper left of the text block, with the text column running to its right and continuing full width beneath. Right margin notes beside the column. Below the text: a chapter heading, a title in italics, a large initial paragraph, and continuing text to the foot.

main_text.p: Pharia: quasi dixerit Cererē, quæ in Ægypto. Et intellegi credam Isidem: quę nomine diuertit à Cerere, numine communicat. Ità Herodotus: Δημήτρ δἐ, Ισις. In Apuleio, ipsa de se Isis: Me primigenij Phryges Pessinuntiam matrem nominant, me Eleusinij vetustam deam Cererem. Eusebius de Præparatione: Φασὶ τὸν Αἰγυ-πτιοι τὸν μὲν Ὀσιριν εἶναι τὸν Διόνυσον, τὸν δὲ Ισιν τὸν δἠμητρα: Aiunt Ægyptij Osirim esse Bacchum, Isidem vero Cererem.
main_text.head: CAP. VI.
Altera Simplicis Crucis species, Infixio. Seneca, Hesychius, Plato, Plinius, illustrati.
main_text.p: ATQVE hæc fuit in Simplici Cruce Affixio: Est & in eâdem Infixio, qualis? cum nudum hominem erecto acuto stipiti infigebant, eâ formâ & facie quam exempla hæc docebunt. Seneca: Consolat. ad Marc. cap. xx.Video istic Cruces nec unius generis, sed aliter ab aliis fabricatas. Alij capite conuerso in terram suspendere,
Lib. xr. de Asin. — Lib. xi. cap. i.

page.notes: Left margin: "Ceres Pharia, siue Aegyptia." and "Infixio, quæ vulgò Impalutio." Right margin: "Lib. xr. de Asin." and "Lib. xi. cap. I." and "Consolat. ad Marc. cap. xx." Several right-margin references are partly illegible in the scan. The Greek in the Eusebius passage and the printed hyphens are reproduced as far as the scan allows; the Herodotus Greek line is doubtful. The woodcut is an engraving of a figure on a cross and is not transcribed.
